newsitem.title: GERMANY: Revaluation transfer to take place in 98 - Bonn.
newsitem.headline: Revaluation transfer to take place in 98 - Bonn.

text.p: The German Finance Ministry confirmed on Thursday that profits from a planned revaluation of the Bundesbank's currency reserves would be transferred in 1998 to a government fund for servicing debt.

Responding to reporters questioning why the date of the transfer was not in a statement issued by Finance Minister Theo Waigel and Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer, a ministry spokeswoman confirmed the move would take place next year.
The move had been widely expected to take place in 1998 under a compromise deal between Waigel and Tietmeyer agreed earlier this month.
But the omission of the date from the statement prompted reporters to question if there had been in a change in the plan.
The spokeswoman also said that, as far as she knew, the main content of Thursday's discussions had concerned the central bank's currency stocks rather than its gold reserves.

Separately, German government coalition sources told Reuters that the Waigel and Tietmeyer agreed that the Bundesbank would in future assess its dollar reserves using an exchange rate of at least 1.50 marks.
This would mean that the central bank would transfer to Bonn an additional 11-13 billion marks in profits in 1998.
The additional profit from the Bundesbank would go to pay off outstanding debt from the former East Germany, which Bonn took over after German unification in 1990.
The central bank's dollar reserves are currently valued at 1.3620 marks, which gives the Bundesbank's dollar reserves a total value of 72.3 billion marks.
